subject: Post-call: Cloudscale latency/throughput eval — proposed A/B plan and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@cloudscale.com>, Bob Lang <bob.lang@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Cloudscale latency/throughput eval — proposed A/B plan and next steps

Hi Alice / Bob,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking us through your inference goals. Quick recap + a concrete A/B proposal so we can lock the lab window and success criteria.

Key points from call (high level):
- Primary goal: validate p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec for your 3 conversational workloads (short prompts, multi-turn chat, long-form summarization).
- Baseline: you currently route to HyperscaleX endpoints; you want an apples-to-apples run versus Redwood hosted + a Dedicated-like config.
- Constraints: 90k token/day test cap for the initial window; test dataset must contain 3k representative requests you agreed to provide.

Why Redwood is worth testing (differentiators we discussed):
- Unified runtime with automatic KV/prefix caching to reduce token generation for multi-turn chat.
- Continuous batching that preserves p95 SLOs while improving throughput for high concurrency.
- Ability to pin model variants and fallback automatically (helps reliability when HyperscaleX throttles).

Proposed A/B plan (draft):
1) Objective metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), median and 95th tokens/sec sustained, 99th tail CPU/GPU utilization, and overall token cost.
2) Environments: 
   - Arm A: your current HyperscaleX endpoint (config you currently use).
   - Arm B: Redwood hosted inference with the same model family (we'll run both default and a quantized variant).
3) Dataset: your 3k sample (short/multi-turn/long). We'll randomize order and run 3 passes per arm to reduce noise.
4) Success criteria (example): Redwood p95 within 15% of HyperscaleX and tokens/sec >= HyperscaleX OR unit token cost < HyperscaleX by 20% while p95 within 25%.
5) Run length: 90 minutes per pass, 3 passes per arm (total 6 windows) — we can compress if you prefer a shorter run.
6) Observability: We'll stream logs to a shared project and provide a runbook (attached) with dashboards for p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

Ask from Cloudscale:
- Share the 3k sample (or a Hub link) by Friday EOD so we can stage the dataset.
- Confirm two candidate 2-hour windows next week for the lab.

Attachments: cloudscale-sample-promptset.json (placeholder) and redwood-inferops-runbook.pdf (runbook + metric definitions).

If this looks good, we’ll schedule the first window and Karthik will send the test harness details (auth, endpoints, and perf script).

Thanks,
Naomi

1) For p99 are you measuring server-side processing only (we'll strip network latency), or end-to-end from our app gateway? We need to be explicit because HyperscaleX reports both.
2) When you say "quantized variant" — can you confirm expected model parity (accuracy) and whether the run will use Redwood Dedicated pools or hosted? We want the closest configuration to our production path.
3) Do you have an estimate of the token-cost delta for the 3k sample (rough ballpark)? This will help get internal buy-in.

We can share the 3k sample (redacted PII) — Alice will upload by EOD Thursday. Candidate windows: Apr 24 14:00–16:00 PDT or Apr 25 10:00–12:00 PDT. Prefer the 24th if you can run.

Hi all — quick technical clarifications and the concrete test harness plan from an ops perspective.

On the Bob questions:
- p99: we'll capture both server-side processing time (token generation start->end on the instance) and an optional E2E measurement if you want to route through your gateway. For apples-to-apples with HyperscaleX I recommend server-side for the initial run and E2E as a follow-up.
- Quantized parity: for the models you flagged (code-nl-3b equivalent in our catalog), our 8-bit quant variant historically shows ~<1% delta on the summary/few-shot tasks we used in past evaluations. We'll provide per-class BLEU/ROUGE diffs after the first pass.
- Dedicated vs hosted: we'll run the hosted configuration that most closely mirrors Dedicated (same GPU class + batching settings). If you want a true Dedicated test later we can schedule a separate run.

Test harness rundown (what we'll push to you):
- A small runner container (curl-based) that accepts a CSV of request IDs + prompt text, hits the Arm endpoint at configurable concurrency, and records per-request server-side timestamps and token counts.
- Config parameters: concurrency, ramp-up, per-request max tokens, timeout. We'll supply a default YAML.
- Metric calculation: p50/p95/p99 latencies (server-side), tokens/sec (per-second moving window), 99th GPU utilization. We'll publish a script for replicable calculations.

Noise-reduction notes:
- We'll randomize order and do 3 passes per arm (recommended).
- We'll pin one test run as the canonical report (median run by p95).

Operational asks from Cloudscale (to prepare):
1) Provide the 3k sample as S3/Drive link.
2) Provide an endpoint for HyperscaleX we should hit (auth token or short-lived key).
3) Confirm which model name + temperature you want us to mirror.

If Apr 24 14:00 PDT works we can do a dry-run earlier that morning (30 mins) to validate auth and runner config. Marcus, can you own the dry-run and the dashboards?

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
